title: Analyses
intro: An analysis is one way of solving the circuit equations: at DC, in the frequency domain around an operating point, or step by step in time. Each can be written as a dot command in the netlist or as a command of the same name in a .control script, where it can be repeated, swept and measured.

items: Operating Point and DC Sweeps: .op, .dc over sources, resistors and temperature, reading device operating points, and .nodeset and .ic.
AC Analysis and Stability: frequency sweeps, gain and phase, group delay, loop gain and phase margin by Middlebrook's and Tian's methods.
Transient Analysis: time steps, integration methods, initial conditions, breakpoints, and the options that trade speed against accuracy.
Noise Analysis: .noise for small-signal noise spectra and their integrals, per-device contributions, and transient noise.
Fourier, Spectra and Distortion: .four and fourier for harmonics and THD, fft, spec and psd for spectra, windows and resampling, and .disto.
Pole-Zero, Transfer Function and Sensitivity: .pz, .tf and .sens.
S-Parameters and Periodic Steady State: .sp with RF ports and Touchstone output, and the experimental .pss.

blocks.text: Every analysis exists in both forms with the same arguments: .tran 1n 100n in the netlist, tran 1n 100n in a .control block. The dot form runs when the circuit is run (run, or batch mode); the control form runs at that point of the script, and can be called many times with different arguments. Each run creates a new plot (tran1, tran2, ac1 ...) holding its vectors; the newest is the current plot.
